Voaters, how do you deal with the passing of a parent of a best friend?

Remember who they were and what they meant to you. Other people who were close to them are good for this. Laugh about stupid things they did or character flaws. Swap stories about the good and the bad. You might be mad or sad or you might not know what to think. That's OK. Let that out with others. You will also find times where something small brings up a memory of them. Whether it brings up good or bad feelings, appreciate how much they affected your life. Finally, you will probably want some time alone to reflect. You could: hike to the middle of nowhere; go for a drive; spend a night with a bottle; or just cry into a pillow for a while. But above all, think about how they made you(or the world in general) better.
Slowly... Over years. Some days you cry, some you smile. Then it all just becomes numb.
Cry a lot, try to go on with your life, cry some more.

There's no "one size fits all" approach to this, so you'll have to play it by ear, to a certain extent. What I most appreciated was my best friend just being normal, how he always was. Depending on the age and circumstances of the death, your friend may not feel like normal things (fun activities, joking around, etc) are permitted in this difficult time. Having a best friend treat you like they always have helps to make everything feel more normal.
Be supportive, keep cool, don't pity, and be that beacon in the end of tunnel.

For your friend: Just be a friend. When my mother died, I felt like I suddenly had nobody and nobody cared. Just make an effort to hang out with them and ask how they're doing. Encourage them to seek counseling if they need it, and remind them that as bad as it may feel, the feeling won't last forever. Eventually, they will feel better.

For you: Similar things. Take the time to grieve, because if you don't, issues can pop up later down the line. I ended up having horrible problems with hypochondria ten years after the fact. Don't be ashamed to get counseling or to talk to friends about how you feel. Your mental health is important. Don't engage in self-destructive things like cutting, overeating, or abusing substances. They help short-term, but make things much worse long term. Make sure you're getting enough sleep, exercising, getting some sunshine, and meditating if you can- all of those things are proven to help with anxiety and depression.

There's plenty. If you want statistics, a quick search shows this report for the US Dept of Labor, 2009: http://www.consad.com/content/reports/Gender%20Wage%20Gap%20Final%20Report.pdf

At page 13 (17 of the 95 pages PDF) you find a summary:

"Extant economic research has identified numerous factors that contribute to the gender wage gap. Many of the factors relate to differences in the choices and behavior of women and men in balancing their work, personal, and family lives. These factors include, most notably, the occupations and industries in which they work, and their human capital development, work experience, career interruptions, and motherhood. Other factors are sources of wage adjustments that compensate specific groups of workers for benefits or duties that disproportionately impact them. Such factors for which empirical evidence has been developed include health insurance, other fringe benefits, and overtime work.

It is not possible to produce a reliable quantitative estimate of the aggregate portion of the raw gender wage gap for which the explanatory factors that have been identified account. Nevertheless, it can confidently be concluded that, collectively, those factors account for a major portion and, possibly, almost all of the raw gender wage gap."

If you want an analysis of any reality underlying a debate in Politics or Economics, I would recommend the Mises Institute: https://mises.org/library/what%E2%80%99s-behind-gender-wage-gap

The Last Boundary will be a grand strategy game set in the near future, at the dawn of your peoples ascent into a space faring civilization. I hopeto make it as complex as Hearts of Iron and as intricate as Dwarf Fortress.

The player will control all aspects of their civilization. Some things, like the economy, they can only influence, their government type will be a combination of the players influence as well as the sensibilities of their people.

Military will be featured at a, what I think to be, realistic level. I.e. a purely military spacecraft would be an expensive undertaking. In fact, space travel, I.e. the colonisation of new worlds will be very expensive. The first additional world the player colonizes may cause some social problems.

At thats a key element of what I'm going for. The societal challenges your people face internally, as well as the other space faring civilizations.

Thelastboundary.com has been up for a while, charting my very slow pace.
Do you have any thoughts on what the interface will look like?

Somewhat, I'm currently still working on the graphics engine and UI toolkit. Actually, to date, there's more code in the UI than there is in the graphics engine. This is because I know that the interface is a make it or break it for this of game.

Considering the different sections, I think the usual "Military", "Research", "Education", "Diplomacy" to be the core elements to the ui. Because much of the players ability to affect their society and economy is based around legislation and expenditure, these will most likely be options as well.

I've thought of also having different, or slightly different options depending on your government type. So a theocratic government would have differring options to a democratic party system.

Still a bit up in the air.
